title: Role sources and role mapping are declared per provider; the reduced Principal carries the resulting roles array
description: The blueprint contributes the `roleModel` capability by naming the provider-record's `roleSources[]` field (an ordered list of claim paths the session-bridge reads: for example `["realm_access.roles", "resource_access.<clientId>.roles", "groups"]`) and an optional project-authored `enrichPrincipal(principal) -> principal` hook the bridge invokes after populating `roles[]`. The session-bridge walks each `roleSources[]` path against the verified claim record (id_token for OIDC providers, userinfo for oauth2-only providers) and populates `roles[]` with the union of the string values found; a path that resolves to a non-string non-array-of-strings shape is refused with `OAUTH2_ROLES_MALFORMED` and the session is not issued. The blueprint mandates that authorisation decisions above the middleware read `principal.roles[]` and never a raw provider claim; project routes that need role-based gating do so through a project-authored predicate that takes the reduced Principal.
rationale: A capability declaration for `roleModel` on a blueprint whose default behaviour is an empty roles array leaves consumers to gate on a token the provider blueprint never wrote a contract for. Naming `roleSources[]` and the malformed-claim refusal is what turns the token into an apply-time observable.
